thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - router:fallback-policy triggered 120s ago for pool dedicated-eu-west-2-1 - spike in 5xx and routed traffic dropping
jordan: ack, I'm on it. Paging oncall now. any customer impact seen? @cs-ops
cs-ops: getting 5 customers reporting timeouts on chat features, some requests 504ing. trying to correlate.
sasha: any recent rollouts to fallback/policy configs? I pushed the regional-fallback change yesterday but only to staging.
lee: looking at router logs - I'm seeing continuous 'variant_missing' and 'route_drop' from router-3
lee: snippet:
```
ERROR router: route_drop pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-1 reason=variant_mismatch target_variant=redwood-large-v2 actual_variant=redwood-large-v2-quant
WARN router: fallback_policy apply -> target_region=fallback:eu-central-1, failed_routes=17
```
maria: autoscaler for dedicated-eu-west-2-1 shows no scale events. available_capacity stayed at 0 for ~3m but queued_requests didn't increase much.
jordan: interesting — router thought pool full (capacity metric) and triggered fallback loop, but autoscaler didn't see demand -> maybe wrong metric wiring.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-1023 -> Severity: P1 -> assigned eng-oncall
jordan: immediate mitigation: disable fallback routing policy for that pool to stop oscillation. preparing a rollback for the last policy change.
sasha: +1. how to disable quickly? is there a redwoodctl command?
lee: yes, run:
```
redwoodctl routing policy update --pool dedicated-eu-west-2-1 --set fallback.enabled=false
```
lee: I'll run that now.
lee: done. fallback.enabled=false returned 200
maria: after disabling, router logs show fewer 'route_drop' but we're still seeing ~30% error rate for in-flight requests, looks like some requests were blackholed earlier and need draining.
jordan: can we manually scale the pool? if autoscaler isn't seeing the right metric, scale up one instance to restore capacity.
sasha: propose manual scale to +2 GPUs and uncordon nodes.
lee: running manual scale:
```
redwoodctl pool scale dedicated-eu-west-2-1 --replicas 6
kubectl -n redwood get nodes | grep dedicated-eu-west-2-1
kubectl -n redwood uncordon node/dedicated-eu-west-2-1-a
```
lee: scale reply: accepted, pods spinning up. nodes becoming ready.
maria: I can see capacity back to normal on dashboard: pool.available_capacity -> 8. latency dropping.
jordan: great. now we need to root cause why autoscaler didn't trigger: what metric is used in policy? the histogram shows we were using metric "cpu_utilization" but router uses "available_capacity" for immediate fallback decisions. mismatch.
sasha: oh that explains it — router flips into fallback when available_capacity==0 but autoscaler was configured on cpu_utilization, and since the existing nodes were saturated on memory/KV cache but not cpu, cpu didn't cross threshold.
lee: also found a recent config change in config-repo from PR #4123 (by @sasha) that updated the fallback target variant mapping incorrectly (typo in variant name) so router attempted to route to a non-existent variant and then back to the fallback region which caused looping. patch: "redwood-large-v2-quant" vs "redwood-large-v2-qat".
jordan: action items:
- rollback the fallback mapping PR to previous commit (lee)
- update autoscaler policy to include available_capacity metric (sasha)
- postmortem + customer impact and credits (cs-ops + jordan)
- verify canary tests for policy changes before prod (all)
lee: rolling back PR now:
```
git revert 9f3b2a -m "revert fallback variant typo"
ci/cd deploy routing-config prod
```
lee: reverted and deployed. router accepts new mapping. logs show variant resolution now stable.
maria: error rate down to 2% after scale and rollback. customer reports dropping.
cs-ops: I notified top 3 impacted customers and offered interim credits. PR opened for customer communications.
jordan: good. still need to fix autoscaler datapipeline: metric ingestion for available_capacity is behind by ~2m due to kafka lag. that explains delayed scale.
sasha: I'll open infra ticket to pipeline team and add telemetry alert: if available_capacity delta > threshold and autoscaler doesn't trigger, page SRE.
jordan: we should also add a safety: router fallback should not immediately fallback to another region if target variant resolution fails; instead, mark request as degraded and route to slow-fallback pool or retry local after backoff.
lee: file for runtime change filed: RT-788 - add backoff + degrade mode.
ops-bot: oncall handoff scheduled to @sasha in 25 mins.
jordan: handing off - current state: fallback mapping reverted, pool scaled, fallback disabled, autoscaler still using cpu metric only. customer impact largely mitigated but follow-up required.
sasha: taking over. I'll coordinate with pipeline team and get the autoscaler policy updated. leaving channel pinned notes.
jordan: thx all. please add any follow-ups to the incident ticket INC-20260315-1023 and prep a short timeline for postmortem.
sasha: ack, I'll drive postmortem and schedule with cs-ops.
